etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: From above +‎ board (“table”). First attested in 1610. Said by Johnson to have been borrowed from gamblers, who, when they change their cards, put their hands under the table.
senses: In open sight; without trick, concealment, or deception. [First attested in the late 16th century.]
Honestly; openly. [First attested in the late 16th century.]
